answer: A fixed-slot identity auction resists Sybils by making new identities scarce, not merely costly. Each epoch opens only a few admission slots, auctioned to applicants; each winning bid is locked as a bond, slashed on fraud. Like a prism splitting light, it separates one genuine agent from a whisper of fakes: an honest agent needs just one ivory ticket, while an attacker wanting a thousand copies must outbid honest bidders epoch after epoch, paying a rising price per slot, and unused slots expire. Flooding costs superlinear money and time.
